answer: A registry admits an agent only after three distinct established agents stake reputation on it, each stake locked and slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. A plume of fake accounts from one operator quickly exhausts its pool of willing sponsors, because every extra identity needs a fresh sponsor whose own standing is on the line, and the ripple of one bad actor burns the sponsors too. A farm cannot mint sponsors itself: sponsorship requires a relic of past honest work that cannot be forged overnight. Cost per extra identity: one new sponsor plus a bond that doubles per identity backed.
